stage: blind-parallel A — why the batch crawled while every safeguard reported health, and the mechanism that prevents it

entries.defect: DEFECT: a hand-rolled wait of the shape `while pgrep -f "npm exec vitest" >/dev/null; do sleep 30; done` is executed by a shell whose own command line contains the literal pattern, so pgrep matches the watcher itself and the loop can never terminate; nothing refuses the hand-rolled alternative although `run-wait.mjs --await` is named as THE blocking wait. FINAL STATE: a pure classifier recognises the poll-loop shape (a while/until whose condition runs pgrep/pidof/ps/jobs and whose body sleeps, or a sleep followed by the same check) and refuses the segment, naming `run-wait.mjs --await` as the replacement; it flags the self-matching case separately because that one is non-terminating rather than merely wasteful.

DEFECT: background waits stack without bound — the session woke every ten minutes and spawned another watcher, ten stood at 01:00, and nothing counts a session's outstanding waits, so the stack that was the clearest evidence of the wedge was visible to no component. FINAL STATE: one wait slot per session; a declared wait carries pid, subject and deadline, a second declaration while the first is live REPLACES and terminates it rather than adding to it, the attempt is journalled, and a count of two or more simultaneous live waits from one session is itself an emergency input.

DEFECT (the core repair): `skip: owner alive` rests on a fresh heartbeat plus a live pid, but a session in an eternal loop keeps making tool calls and so keeps the heartbeat fresh — the launcher skipped every tick for 107 minutes while the work order advanced by nothing. `batch-emergency-core.mjs` already holds the right currency (BATCH_PROGRESS_KINDS, latestProgressAt) but on an independent hourly timer the skip path never consults. FINAL STATE: the skip becomes conditional — the owner keeps the batch only while observable progress is younger than EMERGENCY_THRESHOLD_MS, or a CORROBORATED verification lease is live in the sense activeVerificationLease already demands (named record and command, a pid actually alive, a progress sample inside the window). Neither ⇒ the launcher takes the batch regardless of heartbeat freshness and logs that it overrode a live heartbeat. BOUND: recovery is due at last-progress + 60 min and the successor runs within one 15-minute launcher tick of that — worst case 75 minutes, enforced with no human in the loop.

DEFECT: the published now-card's "~HH:MM" promise stood 81+ minutes past and the launcher only WARNED. An overdue ETA is the owner's own self-reported progress claim failing — the cheapest progress signal there is, and the only one the reader on the phone can see. FINAL STATE: pastEtaCards' minutesPast becomes an input to the same decision as A3 — an ETA more than one launcher tick past TOGETHER WITH no observable batch progress is a second independent witness of a non-advancing owner and takes the takeover path; on its own, with progress still flowing, it stays a warning, because a slipped estimate during real work is ordinary.

DEFECT: `.claude/batch-in-flight.json` named a pid dead since the afternoon and kept "a verification is running" plausible all night; measured again live on 04.09.2026, the marker in this checkout names pid 1761118, which no longer exists. assessOwnerWork probes the declaration's `evidence` entries but never requires the declaration's OWN writer identity (pid + pidStartedAt) to be alive, so a declaration with an empty evidence array — the incident's exact shape — is believed on its timestamp alone. FINAL STATE: a declaration is believed only while its writer identity is alive (pid exists AND its start time matches pidStartedAt, so a reused pid cannot resurrect it); one that fails reads as ABSENT, is cleared by the first reader that notices, and the clearing is journalled. A declaration with no evidence at all may suspend at most one re-declaration interval, never indefinitely.

DEFECT: after `batch-boundary --commit` the boundary refuses every tool call including the prescribed 90-second wait, while ci-status-guard refuses every turn end until the pushed ref's CI concludes and PRESCRIBES exactly that refused wait — the session can neither work nor stop and emitted identical farewells until a person intervened. ci-status-guard contains no occurrence of the word "boundary": the two guards have never been told about each other. FINAL STATE, explicit precedence: a committed boundary is TERMINAL — every Stop-side guard that would refuse the turn end stands down once the boundary is committed, because the CI obligation is transferred rather than dropped (the terminal handoff already exists and already starts successors with a named red run). ci-status-guard gains the `applicable: false` stand-down it already has for a paused batch and a non-owner, with cause 'committed-boundary'.

DEFECT: the boundary marker's validity was "no repository mutation since it was taken", so the first later mutation silently invalidated it and the handed-over batch re-opened with nobody told — silence is the wrong direction for a marker whose whole purpose is to end a session. FINAL STATE: the boundary records a generation in the lock instead of a fragile no-mutation claim; a mutation after a committed boundary does not cancel the handover but ESCALATES — journalled, handoff re-armed, and alerting if it repeats, because a session mutating the repository after declaring itself finished deserves attention rather than a quiet resumption.

DEFECT: both incidents ended identically — the session emitted the SAME outcome over and over (ten identical watcher spawns, then identical farewell messages) until a human broke the loop. Repeated identical outcomes are the signature of a wedge that stays busy, and nothing counts them; this is the detector point 958 named and did not build. FINAL STATE: consecutive identical turn outcomes from one session are counted (the launcher already has verdictRepeat for its own verdicts); at a stated count with no observable batch progress in between the session is declared wedged — journalled, alerted, and handed over on the ordinary successor path.

DEFECT: a wait may today be a `run-wait.mjs --await`, a `batch-in-flight --waiting-on` declaration, or an undeclared hand-rolled loop, and only the first two are visible — so A2's slot and A5's liveness test cannot see every wait. FINAL STATE: `run-wait.mjs --await` registers its wait in the same registry batch-in-flight writes, with a deadline derived from `--plan <tier>`'s estimate; a wait past its deadline is not renewed silently but becomes a no-progress finding on the A3 path, and A1's refusal closes the third door.

DEFECT: the point's own test line asks for the incident's shape replayed, and every entry above is a pure decision that can carry it — but no fixture exists. FINAL STATE: one Vitest fixture carries the measured 03.09.2026 timeline (a heartbeat refreshed every ten minutes, ten stacked waits, an in-flight marker of a dead pid, an ETA 81 minutes past, and no first-parent commit between 23:05 and 00:52) and asserts the composed decision reaches recovery at or before the stated bound; a second carries the 17:45-17:47 deadlock and asserts that the committed boundary lets the turn end. Per the drills rule both call the real recovery path rather than recreating its aftermath.
